Ravi / Maya — thanks for the note and for surfacing this early. Quick summary of Redwood's suggested compromise so we can move to contracting:

- Onboarding tolerance: for the first 60 days after production cutover we propose an operational allowance for batched inference where the formal uptime anchor is 99.7% (versus standard 99.9%). This accounts for cache warm-up and model optimization windows.

- Phased uplift: months 61–90 move to 99.85%, and month 91+ revert to the standard 99.9% availability commitment.

- Monthly remedy (service credits): sliding scale tied to the month-end measured availability (calculated against serviceable minutes):
  * 99.9% and above: no credit
  * 99.5%–99.899%: 10% of monthly invoice
  * 99.0%–99.499%: 25% of monthly invoice
  * <99.0%: 50% of monthly invoice (cap: 100% of that month's invoice)

- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows (we propose 2 x 2-hour windows / month for critical kernel upgrades) and agreed third‑party infra provider outages are carved out.

I attached an initial redline of our standard SLA showing the proposed language. Please review and flag anything materially blocking for Octave. If acceptable, we can route the final through DocuSign.

Next steps I suggest: Maya/Procurement provide any redline points; Laura will review legal language; Ben will prepare pricing impact notes if you need to treat this as a commercial concession.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jonas — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of comments from our side after an initial pass (procurement + legal):

1) We can't accept a 60-day window at 99.7 without a clearer transitional metric. Proposal: 90-day staged approach where months 1–30 days: 99.5% (warm-up), days 31–60: 99.7%, days 61–90: 99.85%, month 91+: 99.9%.
2) The credit bands are fine but Procurement needs a cap and a deterministic calculation. Suggested deterministic formula: Credit = (1 - measured_availability) * monthly_recurring_fee, rounded to nearest dollar, with a monthly cap equal to 50% of the monthly invoice. (Note: this is different to your sliding band approach.)
3) We require availability measurement to be based on a mutually agreed monitoring endpoint (Octave will provide telemetry hooks) and monthly reporting.

I've attached our procurement team's comments as a PDF — it highlights redline passages. If Redwood can accept the 90-day staged approach and the deterministic formula with a 50% cap we can move to final redline this week.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of Procurement | Octave Health

Maya / Ravi — thanks for the clear feedback and the PDF redlines. We discussed internally (legal + commercial) and propose the following final compromise to unblock contracting this week:

1) Staged availability (accepting most of your structure, with a modest commercial concession):
   - Day 0–30: 99.5%
   - Day 31–60: 99.7%
   - Day 61–90: 99.85%
   - Day 91+: 99.9% (standard commitment)

2) Deterministic credit formula (harmonized):
   - Primary calculation: Credit = (1 - measured_monthly_availability) * monthly_recurring_fee, rounded to nearest dollar.
   - Floor remission: for availability >= 99.9% — no credit.
   - Monthly cap: credits capped at 50% of the monthly invoice for each billing period.
   - For commercial simplicity, when availability falls into extreme outage (<95%) we will also open a remedial operational post‑mortem and offer a one-time service credit equal to 100% of the monthly recurring fee as an extraordinary remedy (requires joint verification).

3) Measurement and transparency:
   - We accept Octave telemetry hooks and will publish a monthly availability report to the shared Drive link and include raw minute-level availability for dispute windows.

4) Maintenance carveouts and emergency operations — we will keep standard carveouts (scheduled maintenance with 48h notice, catastrophic provider outages) and will include a maximum of two maintenance windows per calendar month unless mutually agreed otherwise.

If that aligns with Octave's risk appetite we will:
- Incorporate the language into the SLA redline (Laura),
- Produce a final commercial summary for Finance (Ben), and
- Send DocuSign for signature.

Please confirm and we will move to final execution.
